slides.title: Corporate output, compensation and valuation
slides.context: 2009–2024. 16 complete annual observations from the preserved September 2026 package
slides.takeaway: 2024 is the latest common year in this data package. Every displayed year enters the fit.

slides.title: Labor quantities and the wage bridge
slides.context: 2009–2024. BA+ skilled labor and non-BA unskilled labor in CPS private-for-profit employment
slides.takeaway: The bridge exactly allocates total compensation, but the skill-specific annual bills remain inferred.

slides.title: External parameters and normalizations
slides.context: 2009–2024. The external benchmark and the higher-markup diagnostic have different roles
slides.takeaway: ρ = 2 respects complementarity. Its capital–labor literature basis is an analogy for the V6 input margin.

slides.title: P1: production and research allocation
slides.context: 2009–2024. Baseline μ = 1.61 and diagnostic μ = 3.5 use the same measured panel
slides.takeaway: The baseline fails in all 16 years. Later steps proceed only in the explicitly labelled diagnostic case.

slides.title: P2: a constant innovation productivity
slides.takeaway: The sequential estimate is a = 0.003085. Relative valuation RMSE is 31.30%.

slides.title: P2: knowledge growth and accumulation
slides.takeaway: The joint estimator uses the innovation-law path N(a). The valuation-implied path remains a diagnostic.

slides.title: P4: effective CES coefficients
slides.takeaway: The two coefficients identify datewise augmentation only after fixing α. They reuse the wage and output data.

slides.title: P5: sequential spillover estimates
slides.context: 2009–2024. Conditional diagnostic: μ = 3.5, θ = 0.2857, ρ = 2. Fifteen transitions from 2009–2010 through 2023–2024
slides.takeaway: The sequential estimates already fail the ordering: ξ = -0.2536 and ν = 2.3285.

slides.title: Productivity scales over the sequential path
slides.context: 2009–2024. Conditional diagnostic: μ = 3.5, θ = 0.2857, ρ = 2. Sequential NQ, ξ and ν enter this phase
slides.takeaway: Full-sample log intercepts use all dates. The initial-date inversions remain a useful comparison.

slides.title: Joint production fit
slides.takeaway: The joint fit uses each structural restriction once. It profiles a and fits both technology regressions.

slides.title: Targeted fit and an untargeted cash-flow check
slides.takeaway: Good production fit coexists with large valuation and cash-flow errors. No holdout or GE validation is available.

slides.title: The relative-wage restriction reverses the ordering
slides.takeaway: The relative-input term contributes 95.9% of the negative fitted gap. This is an algebraic decomposition.

slides.title: Mapping changes alter levels but preserve ξ < ν
slides.takeaway: Fixing labor stocks makes ξ positive. None of the ten tested mappings or counterfactuals restores the ordering.

slides.title: The restricted fit reaches equal spillovers
slides.takeaway: The best closed-cone fit reaches ξ = ν. Equality still violates the strict unbalanced-growth primitive.

slides.title: P3: an alternative joint markup route
slides.context: 2009–2024. This exercise frees θ and a and does not replace the external benchmark
slides.takeaway: The fitted positive slope implies a negative inverse markup. P3 also fails economic admissibility.

slides.title: Parameter ledger and current calibration status
slides.context: 2009–2024. US conditional production block. Full two-country equilibrium remains outside this run
slides.takeaway: No admissible baseline vector emerges. The next empirical step is matched factor quantities and compensation.
